title: Strainer: Encrypted Video Traffic Identification for Mixed Segment Transmission Pattern

problem.claim: Identifying the video source of encrypted video traffic is a critical network-regulation task.

gap.claim: Under DASH, mixed segment transmission patterns make fingerprint matching difficult, particularly in poor networks.

contributions.claim: Strainer is a DASH TLS-encrypted video traffic identification method tailored to mixed segment transmission patterns.
The Chunk Decomposition Model uses localized preliminary imitation-learning training followed by global reinforcement-learning optimization training.
CDM decomposes traffic fingerprints into segment sequences to enable distance computation with video fingerprints and improve fingerprint-matching efficiency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that precise chunk sizes can be extracted from the TLS record layer of video traffic.
The authors report significant performance improvement over six state-of-the-art methods across six scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Encrypted video traffic source identification is important for network regulation.
DASH mixed segment transmission patterns hinder fingerprint matching, especially in poor networks.
Strainer addresses the challenge through a DASH TLS-encrypted traffic identification method.
The method extracts precise chunk sizes and uses CDM with imitation learning and reinforcement learning to decompose traffic fingerprints into segment sequences.
Strainer is reported to improve performance over six state-of-the-art methods across six scenarios.
